answer: In an agent economy, each identity must sustain a live beacon that periodically signs a rolling hash of its own prior interactions with a cryptographic quill. Honest agents recycle the same key and history cheaply, but a Sybil attacker must mint a fresh beacon and forge a unique interaction chain for every fake head, locking progressive nectar deposits that scale with the number of concurrent beacons and the depth of the forged history—making large farms pay superlinear compute and capital costs that honest single agents never face.
